page: Microsoft Azure HB368-336rs_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the HBv5 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 336 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. The system is equipped with 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.33 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 15,851 GB NVMe SSD.

This server configuration is RDMA capable and supports Premium Storage. It does not include any graphics processing units. The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff: while it offers a massive allocation of dedicated compute cores and high-capacity local NVMe storage, the memory-to-core ratio is relatively low at 1.33 GB per core, which limits its applicability for memory-intensive workloads that require large datasets to be held entirely in RAM per thread.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the HB368-336rs_v5 provides high compute density and substantial local storage capacity on a single instance, reducing the need for multi-node clustering for certain large-scale tasks. It is designed for high-performance computing workloads, large-scale parallel processing, compute-heavy simulations, and storage-intensive database operations that can leverage the massive NVMe SSD capacity and RDMA networking capabilities.
